options: A. Create a prompt template that teaches the LLM to detect attack patterns.

questions.questionText: A company intends to add generative AI capabilities to its application by integrating a large language model (LLM). The LLM responses must be as deterministic and stable as possible. Which solution fulfills these requirements?
options: A. Configure the application to automatically set the temperature parameter to 0 when submitting the prompt to the LLM.
B. Configure the application to automatically add "make your response deterministic" at the end of the prompt before submitting the prompt to the LLM.
C. Configure the application to automatically add "make your response deterministic" at the beginning of the prompt before submitting the prompt to the LLM.
D. Configure the application to automatically set the temperature parameter to 1 when submitting the prompt to the LLM.
questions.explanation: Temperature is the inference parameter that controls response randomness. A temperature of 0 minimizes randomness and therefore yields the most deterministic and stable output for the same prompt; instructing the model in prompt text does not provide the same sampling control, while a temperature of 1 increases variation.

This satisfies regulatory compliance requirements that prohibit internet access while allowing the VPC to access Bedrock and other AWS services over AWS's internal network. questions.questionText: A company is introducing a mobile app that helps users learn foreign languages. The app makes text more coherent by calling a large language model (LLM). The company collected a diverse dataset of text and supplemented the dataset with examples of more readable versions. The company wants the LLM output to resemble the provided examples. Which metric should the company use to assess whether the LLM meets these requirements?
options: A. Value of the loss function
C. Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE) score
D. Latency of the text generation
questions.explanation: ROUGE (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation) is specifically designed to measure how well generated text matches reference examples by calculating n-gram overlap, precision, recall, and F1 scores. Since the company has reference examples of readable text and wants the model's output to resemble them, ROUGE directly evaluates this alignment. The loss function measures training performance, semantic robustness measures resilience, and latency measures speed—none assess output similarity to examples.

A prompt and its requested output length must therefore remain within the maximum token count supported by every target model. questions.questionText: A bank has fine-tuned a large language model (LLM) to expedite the loan approval process. How should the bank fix this issue MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Include more diverse training data. Fine-tune the model again by using the new data.
B. Use Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with the fine-tuned model.
C. Use AWS Trusted Advisor checks to eliminate bias.
D. Pre-train a new LLM with more diverse training data.
questions.explanation: The demographic disparity in loan approvals most likely stems from an unrepresentative training set, so augmenting the data with more diverse examples and re-fine-tuning the existing model directly targets the root cause at a fraction of the cost of pre-training a brand-new foundation model. Retrieval Augmented Generation only supplements the model's context at inference time and does not correct bias already learned in the model's weights, and AWS Trusted Advisor has no capability to detect or remediate model bias.

B. Add hyperparameters to the model.

D. Increase the model training time.
questions.explanation: The performance gap between training and production typically indicates overfitting—the model learned training data too closely and fails to generalize. questions.questionText: A company is developing a chatbot that uses a large language model (LLM) to respond to customer product questions. The company wants the chatbot to answer product questions only and not respond to questions about any other topics. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Set guardrails on the LLM prompt template.
B. Write custom application logic to identify questions about other topics.
C. Reduce the information the LLM can access.
D. Set the temperature parameter value to a lower number.
questions.explanation: LLM guardrails can define and block undesirable or denied topics in user inputs and model responses, providing managed enforcement of a product-only scope. Custom application logic requires ongoing development and maintenance; restricting information access does not prevent responses based on the model’s general knowledge, and temperature controls randomness rather than topic boundaries.

questions.questionText: A company is building an agent for its application using Amazon Bedrock Agents. The agent is performing well, but the company wants to improve the agent’s accuracy by supplying specific examples. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Modify the advanced prompts for the agent to include the examples.
B. Create a guardrail for the agent that includes the examples.

D. Run a script in AWS Lambda that adds the examples to the training dataset.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Agents advanced prompt templates support hand-curated examples for few-shot prompting, which improves model accuracy for a specific task. Adding the examples to the agent’s advanced prompts therefore meets the requirement.

questions.questionText: Which option is a characteristic of AI governance frameworks that build trust and enable the deployment of human-centered AI technologies?
options: A. Expanding initiatives across business units to create long-term business value
B. Ensuring alignment with business standards, revenue goals, and stakeholder expectations
C. Overcoming challenges to drive business transformation and growth
D. Developing policies and guidelines for data, transparency, responsible AI, and compliance
questions.explanation: AI governance frameworks define policies and guidelines that govern data practices, transparency, responsible AI, accountability, and compliance. These controls help ensure that AI systems are trustworthy, ethical, and human-centered throughout their lifecycle.
learnMore: Govern AI — Cloud Adoption Framework
Guidance to set your organization's responsible AI policies

questions.questionText: A company has developed multiple ML models. The company requires a solution to store, manage, and version the models. Which AWS service or feature satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Model Registry catalogs ML models and manages their versions, metadata, lifecycle stages, and approval status through model groups and versioned model packages.

questions.questionText: A company wants to use AI for budgeting. It created one budget manually and another by using an AI model. The company compared the budgets to assess the AI model’s performance. The AI-model budget contained incorrect numbers. Which option represents the AI model’s problem?
questions.explanation: Hallucinations occur when an AI model generates incorrect or fabricated information, such as inaccurate budget figures.
learnMore: Minimize generative AI hallucinations with Automated Reasoning checks (AWS)

questions.questionText: AWS Certified AI Practitioner AIF-C01 By Amazon · Question Mode
options: A. To authenticate user credentials to access responses from AI

C. To define the role and behavioral boundaries of AI

Configure advanced prompts (Amazon Bedrock)

For 5-year retention at the lowest cost, Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically transitions logs between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on usage patterns, optimizing costs over time. questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: AWS Certified AI Practitioner AIF-C01 By Amazon · Question Mode
questions.explanation: Business goal identification, the first phase of the ML lifecycle, is where compliance and regulatory requirements are determined. At this stage, organizations define project scope and constraints, including legal obligations (GDPR, HIPAA, etc.), ethical considerations, and industry-specific regulations. These requirements then inform all subsequent phases. While data collection involves compliance execution, the strategic determination of what regulations apply occurs at project initiation.

questions.questionText: AWS Certified AI Practitioner AIF-C01 By Amazon · Question Mode
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock provides managed access to foundation models for building generative-AI applications, including applications that generate product descriptions and personalized recommendations using customer-location context. Amazon Macie is for sensitive-data discovery, Amazon Transcribe is for speech-to-text, and Amazon Textract extracts document content.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: AWS Certified AI Practitioner AIF-C01 By Amazon · Question Mode
options: A. Analyze cost and usage reports in AWS Cost Explorer.
B. Download AWS security and compliance documents from AWS Artifact.
C. Configure Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to restrict discoverable FMs.
D. Build a hybrid search solution by using Amazon OpenSearch Service.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: AWS Certified AI Practitioner AIF-C01 By Amazon · Question Mode
questions.explanation: Adversarial prompting involves deliberately crafting potentially harmful prompts to expose vulnerabilities and weaknesses in an AI system's safety mechanisms. This proactive security testing approach helps identify and remediate susceptibilities to prompt injection attacks before deployment. Zero-shot prompting is a simple query technique unrelated to security, least-to-most prompting simplifies task complexity, and chain-of-thought prompting improves reasoning but is not a primary defense against injection attacks.

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon SageMaker AI to produce article summaries in multiple languages. The company requires a metric to assess the quality of those summary translations across multiple languages. Which evaluation metric meets these requirements?
options: A. Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE)
C. Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC)
questions.explanation: BLEU evaluates machine translation quality by measuring n-gram overlap between generated text and reference translations. AWS documentation identifies BLEU as commonly used for translation evaluation; ROUGE is chiefly a summarization metric, while AUC and precision assess classification performance.
learnMore: Evaluating your SageMaker AI-trained model - Amazon Nova

questions.questionText: A law firm wants to build an AI application by using large language models (LLMs). The application will read legal documents and extract key points from the documents. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Build an automatic named entity recognition system.
D. Develop a multi-language translation system.
questions.explanation: A summarization chatbot condenses lengthy legal documents into key points while preserving essential information. Named entity recognition identifies specific entities like names and dates but does not provide comprehensive key point extraction; recommendation engines and translation systems are unrelated to the stated requirement.
learnMore: Text summarization in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company wants to evaluate internet quality in remote areas around the world. The company must collect internet-speed data and store it in Amazon RDS. The company will analyze how internet speed varies throughout each day. The company wants to build an AI model to predict possible internet disruptions. Which type of data should the company collect for this task?
questions.explanation: Time series data records observations with timestamps in chronological order. Repeated internet-speed measurements can capture intraday patterns and changes over time, enabling a forecasting model to predict potential disruptions. AWS defines time-series data as observations or measurements recorded over regular time intervals, with each observation associated with a timestamp or time period.

questions.questionText: A company is deploying AI/ML models using AWS services. The company wants to provide transparency into the models’ decision-making processes and explanations of model outputs. Which AWS service or feature fulfills these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards provide a standardized way to document a model’s intended use, training and evaluation details, performance, limitations, and other governance information, supporting transparency for AI/ML models.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service offers a broad selection of high-performing generative AI foundation models (FMs)?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed AWS service that provides secure access to high-performing foundation models from leading AI companies for building generative AI applications.

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock re-ingestion includes parsing, chunking, generating embeddings, and indexing into the vector store. RAG is a retrieval pattern used after the knowledge base has been ingested, not an ingestion step.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: How can companies use large language models (LLMs) securely on Amazon Bedrock?
options: A. Design clear and specific prompts. Configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles and policies by using least privilege access.
B. Enable AWS Audit Manager for automatic model evaluation jobs.
C. Enable Amazon Bedrock automatic model evaluation jobs.
D. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to make models explainable and to monitor for bias.
questions.explanation: Securing LLMs on Amazon Bedrock requires two complementary approaches: first, designing clear and specific prompts reduces the risk of unintended or harmful outputs by guiding model behavior; second, configuring IAM roles with least privilege access ensures only authorized users and services can invoke the models. The other options (Audit Manager, automatic evaluation jobs, CloudWatch Logs) address monitoring or auditing, not security controls.
learnMore: Identity and access management for Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company has built an image classification model to predict plant diseases from photos of plant leaves. The company wants to evaluate how many images the model classified correctly. Which evaluation metric should the company use to measure the model's performance?
questions.explanation: Accuracy measures the proportion of correctly classified instances out of all instances, making it the ideal metric for evaluating how many images a classification model predicted correctly. This metric is straightforward and directly answers the business question when classes are reasonably balanced. R-squared and RMSE are regression metrics, while learning rate is a hyperparameter, not an evaluation metric.
learnMore: Evaluating model accuracy
SageMaker classification metrics

questions.questionText: A company has documents that are missing some words because of a database error. The company wants to build an ML model that can suggest potential words to fill in the missing text. Which type of model meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: BERT-based models excel at predicting masked words in text through bidirectional context understanding—a technique called masked language modeling. This makes them ideally suited for text completion and word prediction tasks. Other options fail: topic modeling categorizes documents but doesn't predict words; clustering groups data without generating predictions; prescriptive models recommend actions rather than fill text.

This approach ensures the model performs equitably across diverse demographic groups, reducing algorithmic bias and discrimination. Explainability (B) concerns model decision transparency, governance (C) involves oversight processes, and transparency (D) means being open about limitations—none directly address the diversity approach shown.

questions.questionText: AWS Certified AI Practitioner AIF-C01 By Amazon · Question Mode
options: A. Patching and updating the versions of Amazon Bedrock
B. Protecting the infrastructure that hosts Amazon Bedrock
C. Securing the company's data in transit and at rest
D. Provisioning Amazon Bedrock within the company network
questions.explanation: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, AWS manages patching and infrastructure security for Amazon Bedrock, while customers are responsible for securing their own data both in transit (during transmission) and at rest (in storage). This includes implementing encryption, access controls, and other security measures to protect sensitive data.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: AWS Certified AI Practitioner AIF-C01 By Amazon · Question Mode
options: A. Use Amazon CloudFront to restrict access to the company’s private content.

C. Use AWS Lake Formation to manage centralized data governance and cross-account data sharing.
D. Use AWS PrivateLink to configure a private connection between the company’s VPC and Amazon Bedrock.
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink can create an interface VPC endpoint between a VPC and Amazon Bedrock, allowing private API access without an internet gateway, NAT device, or public IP addresses. This prevents the Bedrock API connection from requiring internet exposure.

options: A. Use Amazon SageMaker and iterate with newer data.

questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker with iterative retraining on newer data enables continuous model improvement. As new sales and waste patterns emerge, retraining the model on updated datasets allows it to adapt and maintain accuracy over time. Personalize (B) optimizes recommendations, CloudWatch (C) provides monitoring but not model improvement, and Rekognition (D) is for image recognition tasks, not time-series forecasting.

questions.questionText: What is continued pre-training?
options: A. The process of fine-tuning a pre-trained language model on labeled data for a specific task
B. The process of providing unlabeled data to a pre-trained language model to improve the model’s domain knowledge
C. The process of training a language model from the beginning on a specific dataset
D. The process of evaluating the performance of a pre-trained language model on a test set
questions.explanation: Continued pre-training further trains an existing language model on unlabeled, usually domain-specific data so that it acquires stronger knowledge of that domain before any task-specific fine-tuning.

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner is developing an ML model and wants to give stakeholders model transparency and explainability. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Present the model Shapley values.
B. Provide the model accuracy measure.
C. Provide the model confusion matrix.
D. Provide a secure model inference endpoint.
questions.explanation: Shapley values attribute a model prediction to its input features, showing each feature’s contribution. They therefore provide model transparency and explainability.

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon Bedrock to build an AI assistant that helps customers locate relevant products through suggestions. However, the AI assistant’s responses are frequently generic and irrelevant. The company wants to apply prompt engineering to improve the AI assistant’s responses. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use few-shot prompting to add domain-specific context and explicit instructions.
B. Use chain-of-thought prompting with hidden reasoning steps to ignore explicit domain instructions.
C. Modify the AI assistant's conversational style to use more formal language and include technical product specifications.
D. Use zero-shot prompting to augment retrieval from a product database.
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting can provide representative domain examples alongside clear task instructions and product context, conditioning the model to produce more relevant, use-case-specific recommendations. Amazon Bedrock guidance identifies instructions, domain context, and demonstration examples as prompt components, and notes that few-shot examples can improve response performance.

questions.explanation: AWS Audit Manager supports ongoing audit and compliance work by collecting evidence against prebuilt or custom frameworks and controls for regulations and internal requirements. questions.questionText: A company is rolling out a new feature for its application. The feature will refine the style of output messages. To implement the feature, the company will fine-tune a large language model (LLM) on Amazon Bedrock. What type of data does the company need to meet these requirements?
options: A. Samples of only input messages
B. Samples of only output messages

D. Separate samples of input and output messages
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock supervised fine-tuning requires labeled examples that connect the input to the desired output. Paired input and output messages teach the model which response style to generate for a given message. Customize your model to improve performance for your use case

questions.questionText: A company trains ML models using datasets in which some classes contain more examples than others. The company wants to assess how effectively the model balances detecting and labeling the classes. Which metric should the company use?
questions.explanation: F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, measuring the balance between finding instances of a class and assigning correct class labels. It is especially useful when class frequencies are imbalanced, where accuracy alone can be misleading.

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner is building a model to generate images of humans in various professions. The AI practitioner discovered that the input data is biased and that specific attributes affect the image generation and create bias in the model. Which technique will solve the problem?
options: A. Data augmentation for imbalanced classes
B. Model monitoring for class distribution
questions.explanation: Data augmentation for imbalanced classes addresses bias in image generation models by artificially increasing the diversity and representation of underrepresented groups or attributes in the training data. By applying transformations (rotations, color jittering, etc.) to expand minority class samples, the model learns more fairly across demographic groups. Model monitoring detects bias post-training, RAG is for retrieval tasks, and watermark detection verifies image provenance—none directly mitigate training data bias.

questions.questionText: A company is developing a model to label credit card transactions. It has a large quantity of sample transaction data to train the model, but most of this transaction data is unlabeled. The data contains no confidential information. The company must obtain labeled sample data to fine-tune the model. Which solutions meet these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Run batch inference jobs on the unlabeled data.
B. Run an Amazon SageMaker AI training job that uses the PyTorch Distributed library to label data.
C. Use an Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth labeling job with Amazon Mechanical Turk workers.
D. Use an optical character recognition model trained on labeled samples to label unlabeled samples.
E. Run an Amazon SageMaker AI labeling job.
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth labeling jobs can use Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to generate human labels, provided the data is appropriate for a public workforce. SageMaker AI labeling jobs can create labeled datasets, including by using Ground Truth automated data labeling for supported large datasets. These outputs can be used to fine-tune a model.

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner observes that a large language model (LLM) produces different responses to the same input over multiple invocations. Which AI risk does this represent?
questions.explanation: Nondeterminism is output variability: the same model input can yield different generated responses across runs. A deterministic model, by contrast, always produces the same output for the same input.

questions.questionText: A financial company uses a generative AI model to set credit limits for new customers. The company wants to make the model’s decision-making process more transparent to its customers. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Use a rule-based system instead of an ML model.
B. Apply explainable AI techniques to show customers which factors influenced the model’s decision.
C. Develop an interactive UI for customers and provide clear technical explanations about the system.
D. Increase the accuracy of the model to reduce the need for transparency.
questions.explanation: Explainable AI techniques expose the factors and feature contributions that influenced a model’s credit-limit decision, enabling customers to understand the basis for that decision.

questions.questionText: A company needs to identify customer groups based on customers’ demographics and purchasing patterns. Which algorithm should the company use to satisfy this requirement?

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: An AI company periodically evaluates its systems and processes with the help of independent software vendors (ISVs). questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for on-demand access to AWS and independent software vendor compliance reports, and it supports email notifications that alert subscribers whenever a new report is published — directly meeting the requirement without any custom integration. AWS Audit Manager assesses the company's own internal control compliance, Trusted Advisor gives cost/performance/security recommendations, and AWS Data Exchange is for subscribing to third-party datasets, none of which deliver ISV compliance-report alerts.

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner intends to use a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, but company leadership believes RAG will make the architecture overly complex. Which response would support the AI practitioner's recommendation to use RAG?
options: A. RAG improves large language model (LLM) inference time.
B. RAG improves model training speed.
questions.explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation grounds LLM responses in retrieved, relevant data, which helps minimize hallucinations and improves factual accuracy. It does not inherently speed model training or inference, and it requires additional retrieval, data, and governance components rather than reducing development controls.

questions.questionText: A company plans to customize Amazon Bedrock foundation models (FMs) to enhance an application's performance. The company needs to prepare a training dataset for fine-tuning a text-to-text model. Which dataset format should the company use to train the models?
options: A. A JSON file with labeled data
B. A CSV file with unlabeled data
C. A CSV file with tabular data
D. A text file with unlabeled data
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock text-to-text fine-tuning uses labeled examples that pair an input prompt with its expected completion. questions.questionText: A company wants to use AI to protect its application from threats. The AI solution needs to check if an IP address is from a suspicious source. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Build a speech recognition system.

D. Create a fraud forecasting system.
questions.explanation: An anomaly detection system identifies patterns and behaviors that deviate from the norm, making it ideal for flagging suspicious IP addresses based on unusual access patterns or traffic anomalies. Speech recognition, NER, and fraud forecasting address different problems; anomaly detection is the correct approach for real-time threat identification.

questions.questionText: A media company wants to analyze viewer behavior and demographics to recommend personalized content. questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously monitors ML models in production and detects drift in model-quality metrics, such as accuracy. questions.questionText: What is the advantage of fine-tuning a foundation model (FM)?

questions.explanation: Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained foundation model to a target task by training it further on labeled examples, improving task-specific performance.

questions.questionText: A company needs to build its own large language model (LLM) based on only the company's private data. The company is concerned about the environmental effect of the training process. Which Amazon EC2 instance type has the LEAST environmental effect when training LLMs?

questions.questionText: Which statement characterizes a generative AI use case for multimodal models?

questions.questionText: Which strategy evaluates the accuracy of a foundation model (FM) that is used in image classification tasks?
options: A. Calculate the total cost of resources used by the model.
B. Measure the model's accuracy against a predefined benchmark dataset.
C. Count the number of layers in the neural network.

questions.explanation: Model accuracy in image classification is evaluated by comparing predictions against ground truth labels in a benchmark dataset, using metrics like accuracy, precision, and recall. This is the standard evaluation methodology for assessing model performance.

C. Use Amazon SageMaker Clarify to compute post-training bias metrics.
D. Use Amazon SageMaker Model Cards to compute post-training bias metrics.
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify computes pre-training bias metrics on raw datasets, allowing potential bias across specified user-group facets to be identified before model training. Post-training metrics evaluate a trained model and its predictions, while Model Cards provide model documentation rather than calculating bias metrics.
learnMore: Pre-training Bias Metrics - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A software development company wants to improve its speed-to-market delivery. It needs a solution that enables developers to generate real-time code and unit tests. Which AWS service fulfills these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Q Developer provides real-time inline code recommendations as developers write code and supports generating unit tests. These capabilities accelerate software development and help reduce time to market.
learnMore: Generating inline suggestions with Amazon Q Developer
Implement practices to improve code quality

questions.questionText: A company plans to use foundation models (FMs) across several use cases, including content summarization, code generation, and AI assistants for customer service. Which solution will implement FMs in the MOST cost-effective way?
options: A. Select the smallest model that meets the performance requirements for each specific use case.
B. Use the largest and most capable model available for all tasks to ensure quality.
C. Build and train a custom FM for each individual use case.
D. Use batch processing for all inference requests to reduce the costs and latency for each request.
questions.explanation: Using the smallest model that satisfies each workload’s performance requirements minimizes inference cost while preserving the necessary quality. Model selection should account for capabilities and cost/throughput; larger or customized models are not inherently cost-effective for every workload. Batch processing is suited to large-scale, non-time-sensitive inference and therefore cannot meet the latency needs of all requests.
learnMore: Model availability & compatibility - Amazon Bedrock
Capacity and Performance - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: An online learning company with a large volume of educational materials wants to implement enterprise search. Which AWS service fulfills these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Kendra is a machine-learning-powered enterprise search service that indexes organizational content and lets users find relevant information using natural-language queries.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company must monitor the performance of its ML systems by using a highly scalable AWS service. Which AWS service fulfills these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch provides scalable monitoring of AWS workloads through metrics, logs, alarms, and dashboards, making it the appropriate service for observing ML system performance.

questions.questionText: A financial company has deployed an ML model to predict customer churn. The model has been in production for 1 week. The company wants to assess how accurately the model’s churn predictions match actual customer behavior. Which metric satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: F1 score is a binary-classification metric that combines precision and recall, measuring how well predicted churn outcomes agree with actual churn outcomes while accounting for both false positives and false negatives.
learnMore: scikit-learn: f1_score

questions.questionText: A food service company wants to gather a dataset to predict customers’ food preferences. The company wants to make sure food preferences from all demographics are represented in the data. Which dataset characteristic is presented in this scenario?
questions.explanation: Diversity in a dataset means including representation from varied demographic groups so that the data reflects different populations and preferences.
learnMore: Pre-training Data Bias - Amazon SageMaker Clarify

questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting supplies several examples that demonstrate the desired task. Chain-of-thought prompting asks for intermediate step-by-step reasoning. Zero-shot prompting requests task completion without example demonstrations.
learnMore: Prompt engineering concepts (Amazon Bedrock)
What is prompt engineering?

questions.questionText: A news agency publishes articles in English and wants to make those articles available in additional languages. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Add Amazon Transcribe to the company’s website.
B. Use the Amazon Translate real-time translation feature.
C. Add Amazon Personalize to the company’s website.
D. Use the Amazon Textract real-time document processing feature.
questions.explanation: Amazon Translate performs on-demand real-time translation of text and documents, including translations from English into supported target languages. It is therefore the appropriate service for making English-language article content available in other languages.
learnMore: Real-time translation - Amazon Translate
Supported languages and language codes - Amazon Translate

questions.questionText: Which option is a benefit of ongoing pre-training when fine-tuning a foundation model (FM)?
options: A. Helps decrease the model's complexity
B. Improves model performance over time
C. Decreases the training time requirement
questions.explanation: Ongoing pre-training during fine-tuning allows a foundation model to continuously learn from new data and evolving contexts. This adaptive process improves the model's ability to handle specific tasks and domains, resulting in better performance over time. Unlike decreasing complexity or training time (which are not primary benefits of ongoing pre-training), enhanced performance through continuous learning is the core advantage.
learnMore: Customize models in Amazon Bedrock with fine-tuning and continued pre-training
Customize your model to improve its performance

questions.questionText: A bank is developing a chatbot to answer customer inquiries about opening a bank account. The chatbot will use public bank documents to generate its responses. The company will use Amazon Bedrock and prompt engineering to enhance the chatbot’s responses. Which prompt engineering technique satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Directional stimulus prompting uses targeted context, cues, and instructions to steer a foundation model toward relevant, domain-specific output. Providing public bank documents as contextual guidance helps constrain responses to the bank’s account-opening information. Amazon Bedrock guidance identifies context as a prompt component that guides how the model uses supplied input when formulating an output.
learnMore: Prompt engineering concepts - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A grocery store wants to build a chatbot that helps customers locate products in the store. The chatbot must check inventory in real time and provide each product’s location in the store. Which prompt-engineering technique should the store use to build the chatbot?
questions.explanation: Reasoning and acting (ReAct) prompting lets a model reason about a request, invoke an external tool or API to retrieve live inventory and location data, and use the returned result to produce its response. This supports answers based on current store information rather than only the model’s existing knowledge.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company is developing an agentic AI application using Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers with the Amazon Q Developer CLI. The company wants to follow MCP security best practices. Which solutions meet these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Keep MCP servers and the Amazon Q Developer CLI updated.
B. Monitor MCP logs for normal successful activity.
C. Use plain text files to store sensitive configurations.
D. Automatically approve all tools that are provided by MCP servers.
E. Install servers only from trusted sources.
questions.explanation: MCP security practices for Amazon Q Developer CLI include keeping MCP servers and the Q CLI updated to receive security fixes, and installing MCP servers only from trusted sources to reduce supply-chain and malicious-server risk. Logs should be monitored for unexpected activity, sensitive configuration should use environment variables, and tools should be reviewed before approval.
learnMore: MCP security - Amazon Q Developer

questions.questionText: Which feature of Amazon OpenSearch Service gives companies the ability to build vector database applications?
options: A. Integration with Amazon S3 for object storage
B. Support for geospatial indexing and queries
C. Scalable index management and nearest neighbor search capability
D. Ability to perform real-time analysis on streaming data
questions.explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service provides built-in k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) search capabilities combined with scalable index management, which is essential for vector database applications. These features enable efficient similarity search on high-dimensional embeddings generated by machine learning models. The other options address different use cases: S3 integration is for object storage, geospatial indexing is for location data, and real-time streaming analysis is for data pipelines—none are specifically designed for vector database functionality.
learnMore: k-NN search in Amazon OpenSearch Service

questions.questionText: A company uses a large language model (LLM) to build a generative AI assistant. To help ensure the assistant produces the most factually accurate responses, the company chooses the Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) technique. Which LLM limitation is the company seeking to reduce?
questions.explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation grounds responses in relevant retrieved source material, which reduces hallucinations—plausible but unsupported or incorrect generated content.
learnMore: What is RAG? (AWS)

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company plans to upload customer-service email messages to Amazon S3 to build a business analysis application. The messages occasionally contain sensitive data. The company wants to be alerted whenever sensitive information is detected. Which solution completely automates the sensitive-data detection process with the LEAST development effort?
options: A. Configure Amazon Macie to detect sensitive information in the documents that are uploaded to Amazon S3.
B. Use Amazon SageMaker endpoints to deploy a large language model (LLM) to redact sensitive data.
C. Develop multiple regex patterns to detect sensitive data. Expose the regex patterns on an Amazon SageMaker notebook.
D. Ask the customers to avoid sharing sensitive information in their email messages.
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie provides managed sensitive-data discovery for Amazon S3 objects and generates sensitive-data findings when it detects sensitive information. Those findings can drive alerting workflows without building or operating a custom model or regex-based detection system.
learnMore: Analyzing findings from automated sensitive data discovery - Amazon Macie
Types of Macie findings

questions.questionText: A company is building an ML model to analyze archived data. The company must perform inference on large datasets that are multiple GBs in size. The company does not need to access the model predictions immediately. Which Amazon SageMaker inference option will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Batch Transform is specifically designed for large-scale batch inference on multi-GB datasets without requiring immediate results. Unlike real-time inference (which needs active endpoints), it processes large volumes efficiently and is the ideal choice for archived data analysis.
learnMore: Batch transform for inference - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.explanation: Privacy and security protects sensitive data and the systems handling it. Fairness requires assessing and mitigating unequal impacts across demographic groups. Robustness concerns reliable, resilient performance when encountering unexpected inputs or conditions.
learnMore: What is Responsible AI? - Azure Machine Learning
Govern AI - Cloud Adoption Framework

questions.questionText: A company has developed a custom model by fine-tuning an existing large language model (LLM) in Amazon Bedrock. The company needs to deploy the model to production and use it to handle a consistent number of requests per minute. Which solution satisfies these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Deploy the model by using an Amazon EC2 compute optimized instance.
B. Use the model with on-demand throughput on Amazon Bedrock.
C. Store the model in Amazon S3 and host the model by using AWS Lambda.
D. Purchase Provisioned Throughput for the model on Amazon Bedrock.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput can be purchased for a custom model and supplies dedicated compute capacity with guaranteed throughput. For a predictable, steady request rate, selecting the needed throughput provides consistent production capacity and can reduce cost compared with pay-as-you-go use at sustained volume.
learnMore: Set up inference for a custom model - Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company is preparing data to fine-tune a large language model (LLM). The company must adhere to responsible AI principles. Which actions satisfy this requirement? Choose two
options: A. Include demographically diverse data sources to improve model fairness.
B. Apply consistent labeling standards across the training dataset.
C. Focus exclusively on high-volume data regardless of quality.
D. Use only synthetic data to train the model.
E. Use fewer labels to reduce ambiguity in data during model training.
questions.explanation: Demographically diverse data sources help make training data more representative and support fairness across groups. Consistent labeling standards improve dataset quality and reduce inconsistent annotations that can introduce bias or unreliable model behavior.
learnMore: Responsible AI - Generative AI Lens
Core dimensions of responsible AI

questions.questionText: A company is developing an ML model to predict customer churn. The model performs well on the training dataset but does not accurately predict churn for new data. Which solution will resolve this issue?
options: A. Decrease the regularization parameter to increase model complexity.
B. Increase the regularization parameter to decrease model complexity.
C. Add more features to the input data.
D. Train the model for more epochs.
questions.explanation: When a model performs well on training data but poorly on new data, it exhibits overfitting. Increasing the regularization parameter penalizes model complexity, reducing the number of features the model relies on and encouraging it to capture general patterns rather than noise. This improves generalization to unseen data. Decreasing regularization or adding more features would worsen overfitting, and additional training epochs would likely reinforce the overfit.
learnMore: What is Overfitting? - AWS
Tune a linear learner model - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A security company uses Amazon Bedrock to run foundation models (FMs). The company wants to make sure that only authorized users can invoke the models. It needs to identify unauthorized access attempts so it can establish appropriate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies and roles for future FM iterations. Which AWS service should the company use to identify unauthorized users attempting to access Amazon Bedrock?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records Amazon Bedrock API calls and their caller identities. Failed Bedrock API calls with errors such as AccessDenied or UnauthorizedOperation reveal unauthorized model-access attempts, enabling the company to refine IAM policies and roles.
learnMore: Monitoring violations - AWS Prescriptive Guidance
Logging IAM and AWS STS API calls with AWS CloudTrail

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company wants to establish one environment for data and AI development. Developers on different teams must be able to access that environment and collaborate. The developers must be able to securely build and share models and generative AI applications in the environment. Which AWS solution satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio provides a unified, governed environment for data, analytics, AI, and ML work. It supports administrator-managed user and group access, collaboration in projects, development and sharing of models, and building and sharing generative AI applications through Amazon Bedrock capabilities.
learnMore: What is Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio?

questions.questionText: A company uses a generative AI (GenAI) system to create medical summaries from patient records. The system occasionally generates inaccurate information that seems credible. Which strategy will mitigate this issue?
options: A. Implement strict input validation and output formatting rules.
B. Implement Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to ground responses.
C. Use smaller, more transparent models for medical applications.
D. Increase computational resources and model size.
questions.explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) retrieves relevant authoritative information from the patient records and uses it as generation context. This grounds summaries in the source data and reduces hallucinated, unsupported statements.

questions.questionText: A company uses a large language model (LLM) on Amazon Bedrock to create a chatbot. The chatbot handles customer support requests. Resolving a request requires several interactions between the customer and the chatbot. Which solution enables the LLM to use content from earlier customer messages?
options: A. Turn on model invocation logging to collect messages.
B. Add messages to the model prompt.
C. Use Amazon Personalize to save conversation history.
D. Use Provisioned Throughput for the LLM.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock preserves conversation context when the application includes the prior conversation messages, with their user or assistant roles, in subsequent model requests. Model invocation logging and Provisioned Throughput do not supply prompt context, and Amazon Personalize does not provide LLM conversation history.
learnMore: Inference using Converse API - Amazon Bedrock

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company stores customer personally identifiable information (PII) data. The company is required to store the PII data within the company's AWS Region. Which governance aspect does this describe?
questions.explanation: Data residency governs where data is physically stored or processed. Requiring customer PII to remain within a particular AWS Region is a data-residency requirement.
learnMore: What is Data Sovereignty?

questions.questionText: A company is using few-shot prompting on a base model that is hosted on Amazon Bedrock. The model currently uses 10 examples in the prompt. The model is invoked once daily and is performing well. The company wants to lower the monthly cost. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Customize the model by using fine-tuning.
B. Decrease the number of tokens in the prompt.
C. Increase the number of tokens in the prompt.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock pricing is token-based, with costs proportional to input and output tokens consumed. Reducing the number of tokens in the prompt (by decreasing examples or making them more concise) directly lowers inference costs per invocation.
learnMore: Prompt engineering concepts (Amazon Bedrock)
Optimize prompt token length

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner is developing software code and wants to rapidly create a test case and documentation for that code. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST effort?
options: A. Upload the code to an online coding assistant.
B. Develop an application to use foundation models (FMs).
C. Use Amazon Q Developer in an integrated development environment (IDE).
D. Research and write test cases. Then, create test cases and add documentation.
questions.explanation: Amazon Q Developer in an IDE can generate unit tests and produce or update code documentation, including READMEs and other documentation, directly from the development environment.
learnMore: Chatting with Amazon Q Developer about code

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon SageMaker for its ML pipeline in a production environment. The company has large input data sizes up to 1 GB and processing times up to 1 hour. The company needs near real-time latency. Which SageMaker inference option meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Asynchronous inference is designed for requests with large payloads (up to 1 GB) and longer processing times (up to 1 hour). The client submits requests to a queue, and results are retrieved asynchronously—this provides near real-time responsiveness to requests without blocking, while real-time inference would struggle with data of this size and complexity.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company plans to collaborate with several research institutes to develop an AI model. The company requires standardized documentation for tracking model versions and maintaining a record of model development. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Track the model changes by using Git.
B. Track the model changes by using Amazon Fraud Detector.
C. Track the model changes by using Amazon SageMaker Model Cards.
D. Track the model changes by using Amazon Comprehend.
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards document key model details throughout the model lifecycle, including training information, metrics, evaluation results, and other governance information. Edits create subsequent, immutable model-card versions, providing a standardized record of model development and changes.
learnMore: Edit a model card

questions.questionText: A company plans to implement a generative AI solution to enhance its marketing operations. The company aims to increase revenue during the next 6 months. Which approach satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Immediately start training a custom FM by using the company's existing data.
B. Conduct stakeholder interviews to refine use cases and set measurable goals.
C. Implement a prebuilt AI assistant solution and measure its impact on customer satisfaction.
D. Analyze industry AI implementations and replicate the most successful features.
questions.explanation: Generative AI initiatives should begin by identifying and refining use cases that align with the business objective and by establishing specific, measurable success criteria. Stakeholder input helps ensure the selected marketing use case is feasible and tied to a revenue outcome within the six-month target period. AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Assessment considerations and prerequisites

questions.questionText: A company wants to explore generative AI applications in an experimental setting. Which solution will satisfy this requirement in the MOST cost-effective way?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock PartyRock is a hands-on, no-code playground for experimenting with and building generative AI applications. AWS provides recurring free daily usage, making it the most cost-effective option for learning and experimentation.
learnMore: PartyRock improves app discovery and announces upcoming free daily use

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner is assessing the performance of an Amazon SageMaker model and must select a performance metric. The metric must display the ratio of correctly classified items to the total number of both correctly and incorrectly classified items. Which metric satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Accuracy measures the proportion of all classifications that are correct: correct classifications divided by the total of correct and incorrect classifications.
learnMore: Accuracy metric - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A company wants to build an AI assistant that allows employees to query internal data. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Q Business is a fully managed generative AI enterprise assistant that can be configured to answer questions using an organization’s connected enterprise data sources.
learnMore: What is Amazon Q Business?

questions.questionText: Which large language model (LLM) parameter determines the number of possible next words or tokens considered at each step in the text-generation process?
questions.explanation: Top K sampling restricts each generation step to the K most likely next tokens, thereby controlling how many candidate tokens are considered. Maximum tokens controls response length, temperature controls sampling randomness, and batch size controls how many inputs are processed together.

questions.questionText: What is tokenization used for in natural language processing (NLP)?
options: C. To break text into smaller units for processing
D. To translate text between languages
questions.explanation: Tokenization splits text into smaller processable units—such as words, subwords, or sentences—that NLP systems can analyze or use as model input.

Detecting syntax

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner needs to fine-tune an open-source large language model (LLM) for text classification. The dataset has already been prepared. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Create a custom model training job in PartyRock on Amazon Bedrock.
B. Use Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to create a training job.
C. Use a custom script to run an Amazon SageMaker AI model training job.
D. Create a Jupyter notebook on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use the notebook to train the model.
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart offers managed, prebuilt workflows for fine-tuning publicly available foundation models, including open-source models. It provisions and runs the training job without requiring a custom training script or self-managed EC2 training environment.
learnMore: SageMaker JumpStart pretrained models
Fine-tune a model in Studio

questions.questionText: A company is training a foundation model (FM). The company wants to increase the accuracy of the model up to a specific acceptance level. Which solution will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Increasing the number of training epochs allows the model to pass through the dataset multiple times, enabling it to learn patterns more thoroughly and improve accuracy up to the acceptance threshold. Each epoch provides additional learning opportunities. Decreasing epochs reduces learning; changing batch size or temperature parameters do not directly target accuracy improvement in the same way.

questions.questionText: A company wants to use a large language model (LLM) on Amazon Bedrock for sentiment analysis. The company needs the LLM to produce more consistent responses to the same input prompt. Which adjustment to an inference parameter should the company make to meet these requirements?
options: C. Decrease the length of output tokens.
D. Increase the maximum generation length.
questions.explanation: The temperature parameter controls randomness in LLM outputs: lower values (approaching 0) make predictions deterministic and consistent, while higher values introduce creativity and variation. For sentiment analysis requiring reliable, repeatable responses to identical prompts, decreasing temperature is the appropriate adjustment. The other parameters affect output length or training behavior rather than consistency.

questions.questionText: A company is building an ML application. The application must automatically group similar customers and products according to their characteristics. Which ML strategy should the company use to satisfy these requirements?
questions.explanation: Unsupervised learning supports clustering, which groups data points with similar characteristics without requiring labeled target outcomes. K-means is a common unsupervised clustering algorithm that forms groups whose members are similar to one another.
learnMore: K-Means Algorithm - Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A company plans to use a large language model (LLM) to generate responses using company data. Which strategy will satisfy this requirement?
options: A. Use first-party pre-trained models from Amazon Bedrock.
B. Use pre-trained open source models.
C. Fine-tune a custom model on company data.
D. Use pre-trained third-party models from Amazon Bedrock.
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning trains a base model on company-provided examples, creating a custom model whose parameters are adapted for the organization’s specific tasks and response patterns. Amazon Bedrock describes model customization as providing training data to improve performance for a specific use case.
learnMore: Customize your model to improve its performance for your use case
Customize a model with fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: A company wants to build an AI solution that generates images and descriptions for a product catalog. The company must choose a foundation model (FM) for this solution. The company must consider each FM's output types. Which FM characteristic is the company assessing?
questions.explanation: Modality describes the types of data a foundation model can accept or produce, such as text and images. A solution that must generate both product images and textual descriptions requires an FM with suitable output modalities.
learnMore: Supported foundation models in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner is creating a prompt for an Amazon Titan model hosted on Amazon Bedrock. The practitioner uses the model to solve numerical reasoning challenges and appends this phrase to the end of the prompt: “Ask the model to show its work by explaining its reasoning step by step.” Which prompt-engineering technique is the AI practitioner applying?
questions.explanation: Chain-of-thought prompting directs a model to work through and explain intermediate reasoning steps, which is particularly useful for numerical and other multi-step reasoning tasks. AWS documents step-by-step reasoning prompts for Amazon Titan as chain-of-thought reasoning.

questions.questionText: A company has developed an AI assistant that gives employees relevant information about internal processes. The AI assistant uses a fine-tuned foundation model (FM). The company wants to use employee feedback to further improve the model’s responses. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: B. Perform continued pre-training and incorporate feedback from employee ratings.
C. Use reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF).
questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) uses human evaluations, such as employee ratings or preferences, as feedback signals to optimize a foundation model toward responses that better match human expectations. AWS describes RLHF as a post-training or fine-tuning technique that aligns an LLM with human preferences and values.

questions.explanation: Model fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model to perform a specific target task with labeled examples. Data augmentation increases the amount and diversity of labeled training data. Continued pre-training uses unlabeled domain data to further adapt a pretrained model’s knowledge and language patterns before downstream tuning.

questions.questionText: A company plans to build an ML model that predicts customer satisfaction. The company requires fully automated model tuning. Which AWS service satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker supports Automatic Model Tuning, also called hyperparameter tuning. It automatically runs multiple training jobs using specified hyperparameter ranges and selects the values that produce the best model according to a chosen metric.
learnMore: Automatic model tuning with SageMaker AI

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company is using custom models in Amazon Bedrock for a generative AI application. The company wants to use a company managed encryption key to encrypt the model artifacts that the model customization jobs create. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
options: A. AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
questions.explanation: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) enables creation and management of customer-managed encryption keys (CMKs) that control encryption of model artifacts. When Amazon Bedrock customization jobs create model artifacts, KMS can encrypt them with company-managed keys, giving the organization full control over key lifecycle and usage. Inspector (B) scans vulnerabilities, Macie (C) discovers sensitive data, and Secrets Manager (D) manages credentials.

questions.questionText: A company needs to generate synthetic-data responses for multiple prompts from a large data volume. The company wants to generate the responses by using an API method. The company does not require the responses immediately. Which solution satisfies these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
options: A. Input the prompts into the model. Generate responses by using real-time inference.
B. Use Amazon Bedrock batch inference. Generate responses asynchronously.
C. Use Amazon Bedrock agents. Build an agent system to process the prompts recursively.
D. Use AWS Lambda functions to automate the task. Submit one prompt after another and store each response.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock batch inference accepts a large set of prompts as a batch job and generates the responses asynchronously. This directly supports high-volume, non-real-time processing through an API without requiring custom sequential orchestration or an agent system. questions.questionText: A company has fine-tuned an Amazon Bedrock foundation model (FM) to generate short document summaries. The company needs an automated metric that compares every model-generated summary with its human-authored reference summary. Which metric satisfies these requirements?
options: B. Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE)
questions.explanation: ROUGE evaluates summarization quality by comparing overlapping word units, such as n-grams or longest common subsequences, between a generated summary and its ground-truth reference summary. AWS documentation identifies ROUGE as a summarization metric for this generated-versus-reference comparison.
learnMore: Accuracy evaluation for summarization — Amazon SageMaker AI

questions.questionText: A design company uses a foundation model (FM) on Amazon Bedrock to create images for a variety of projects. The company wants control over how detailed or abstract each generated image is. Which model parameter should the company change?
questions.explanation: Generation steps control the number of iterative refinement passes used to create an image. More steps generally yield a more detailed, refined result, while fewer steps can yield a simpler or more abstract result.

questions.questionText: An ecommerce company wants to enhance search recommendations by tailoring results to every user of its ecommerce platform. Which AWS service satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize builds personalized recommendations and can tailor user experiences using customer interaction and item data, making it suitable for customized ecommerce search recommendations.

questions.questionText: A research group wants to test different generative AI models for creating research papers. The group has defined a prompt and needs a way to assess the models’ output. The group wants a team of scientists to perform the output assessments. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use automatic evaluation on Amazon Personalize.
B. Use content moderation on Amazon Rekognition.
C. Use model evaluation on Amazon Bedrock.
D. Use sentiment analysis on Amazon Comprehend.
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock model evaluation supports human-based evaluations of generative-model responses. It can use a custom prompt dataset and a work team of employees or subject-matter experts to rate or compare model outputs.

Manage a work team for human evaluations of models in Amazon Bedrock

questions.questionText: Which option represents a disadvantage of using generative AI models in production systems?
options: A. Possible high accuracy and reliability
questions.explanation: Generative AI models can hallucinate, producing inaccurate or fabricated information. This creates reliability and safety risks when their output is used in production systems.

questions.questionText: A social media company wants to use a large language model (LLM) to summarize messages. The company has chosen a few LLMs that are available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. The company wants to compare the generated output toxicity of these models. Which strategy gives the company the ability to evaluate the LLMs with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: C. Model evaluation with human workers
D. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)
questions.explanation: Automatic model evaluation uses predefined metrics and tools to systematically assess model outputs for toxicity and other quality measures with minimal human intervention. This approach dramatically reduces operational overhead compared to crowd-sourcing, which requires many reviewers, or manual human review. questions.questionText: A company operates a website where users make travel reservations. The company wants an AI solution that helps create consistent hotel branding on the website. The AI solution must generate hotel descriptions for the website in a consistent writing style. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock provides access to foundation models for generative text. A text model can be prompted or customized to produce hotel descriptions in a consistent brand writing style. Amazon Comprehend performs natural-language analysis, Amazon Personalize generates recommendations, and Amazon Rekognition analyzes visual content.

questions.questionText: A company is testing the security of a foundation model (FM). During testing, the company wants to get around the safety features and make harmful content. Which security technique is this an example of?
options: A. Fuzzing training data to find vulnerabilities
questions.explanation: Jailbreaking is the security technique of bypassing or disabling the safety restrictions and guardrails placed on a foundation model to make it produce harmful, unintended, or malicious content. Testing a model's robustness through jailbreak attempts is a common security evaluation practice. Fuzzing targets training data, DoS attacks target availability, and penetration testing is a broader security assessment approach.

questions.questionText: A company uses a foundation model (FM) from Amazon Bedrock for an AI search tool. The company wants to fine-tune the model to be more accurate by using the company's data. Which strategy will successfully fine-tune the model?
options: A. Provide labeled data with the prompt field and the completion field.
B. Prepare the training dataset by creating a .txt file that contains multiple lines in .csv format.
C. Purchase Provisioned Throughput for Amazon Bedrock.
D. Train the model on journals and textbooks.
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning foundation models requires labeled training data structured as prompt-completion pairs, where each prompt represents input and completion represents the desired output. This format allows the model to learn patterns specific to the company's use case. CSV files, provisioned throughput, and training on textbooks do not constitute proper fine-tuning data structure.

questions.questionText: A company uses a foundation model (FM) to generate product descriptions. The model occasionally produces inaccurate information. Which potential generative AI risk does this represent?
questions.explanation: Hallucinations occur when a generative AI model produces false, fabricated, or otherwise inaccurate information that is presented as if it were factual.

questions.questionText: A company has implemented a translation tool to help its customer service team address issues from customers worldwide. The company wants to assess the translation tool’s performance. It establishes a parallel data process that compares the tool’s responses with responses from actual humans. Both response sets are generated from the same set of documents. Which strategy should the company use to evaluate the translation tool?
options: A. Use the Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score to estimate the absolute translation quality of the two methods.
B. Use the Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score to estimate the relative translation quality of the two methods.
C. Use the BERTScore to estimate the absolute translation quality of the two methods.
D. Use the BERTScore to estimate the relative translation quality of the two methods.
questions.explanation: BLEU measures the similarity between machine-translated output and high-quality reference translations by comparing matching n-grams. Using the same document corpus and human responses as references enables BLEU scores to compare the translation tool’s quality relative to the human method; BLEU does not provide a reliable absolute measure of translation quality across contexts.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company needs to detect unauthorized API activity for foundation models (FMs) in Amazon Bedrock. Which solution fulfills these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS CloudTrail to monitor API activity.
B. Use AWS Trusted Advisor to monitor model input and output data.
C. Create Amazon QuickSight dashboards to monitor row-level safety.
D. Monitor user access by using Amazon Personalize.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records Amazon Bedrock API calls as events and includes details such as the requesting identity, source IP address, time, and requested action. These audit records can be monitored and analyzed to identify unauthorized API activity.

questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth supports human-in-the-loop labeling to produce high-quality ML training data. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides configurable safety and privacy safeguards for generative AI applications. Amazon SageMaker Clarify detects and measures bias in pre-training data and models.

questions.questionText: A company needs to fine-tune an ML model hosted on Amazon Bedrock. The company plans to use its own sensitive data, which is stored in private databases in a VPC. The data must remain inside the company’s private network. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Restrict access to Amazon Bedrock by using an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) service role.
B. Restrict access to Amazon Bedrock by using an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) resource policy.
C. Use AWS PrivateLink to connect the VPC and Amazon Bedrock.
D. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt the data.
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink provides an interface VPC endpoint that privately connects a VPC to Amazon Bedrock, allowing Bedrock API access without an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN, or public IP addresses. IAM policies control permissions and AWS KMS encrypts data, but neither provides the required private network connectivity.

questions.questionText: An AI practitioner uses Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management to build a reusable prompt. The prompt must be capable of interacting with external services by calling an external API. Which solution meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: A tools configuration defines the tools a compatible model can use while generating a response, enabling the model to invoke an external API capability. Prompt variables provide value substitution, and stop sequences only determine when generation stops.

questions.questionText: An animation company needs to provide subtitles for its content. Which AWS service fulfills this requirement?

questions.questionText: Which machine learning technique uses training data labeled with the correct output values?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning trains a model on input examples paired with their known correct output values (labels).

questions.questionText: A company wants to invoke one Amazon Bedrock endpoint and requires Amazon Bedrock to select the most appropriate foundation model (FM) for each request. The company does not want to hardcode a model. Which Amazon Bedrock feature or resource meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock prompt routing provides one serverless endpoint that dynamically routes each request to a suitable foundation model based on its routing criteria and predicted response quality. It eliminates the need for application-side model-selection logic.

questions.questionText: A company’s large language model (LLM) is experiencing hallucinations. How can the company reduce hallucinations?
options: A. Set up Agents for Amazon Bedrock to supervise the model training.
B. Use data pre-processing and remove any data that causes hallucinations.
C. Decrease the temperature inference parameter for the model.
D. Use a foundation model (FM) that is trained to not hallucinate.
questions.explanation: A lower temperature inference setting reduces randomness by favoring higher-probability token choices, producing more deterministic and predictable model responses. This can reduce hallucinated outputs, although it does not eliminate them entirely.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly characterizes Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)?
options: A. A process that uses large amounts of new data to train large language models (LLMs) to improve LLM performance
B. A process by which large language models (LLMs) reference external authoritative knowledge bases to enhance the relevance and accuracy of LLM responses without re-training
C. A process that limits large language models (LLMs) exclusively to their original training data to improve response speed for business applications without re-training
D. A process that focuses on language translation tasks for businesses that operate in multiple countries
questions.explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation retrieves relevant content from external, authoritative knowledge bases and incorporates it into a model’s response generation. It can improve relevance and factual accuracy without retraining the large language model.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.questionText: A company has deployed an ML model and wants to give external customers secure access to it through the customers’ own applications. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use a custom script in the customers' application for authentication.
B. Store model credentials and share them with the customers directly for authentication.
C. Create a secure API endpoint that customers can use.
D. Embed the model directly into the customers' applications.
questions.explanation: A secure API endpoint exposes the model’s inference capability while keeping the model and its credentials under company control. The endpoint can enforce authentication and authorization for each customer application and protect requests in transit. Amazon API Gateway, for example, supports access-control mechanisms such as JWT authorizers, Lambda authorizers, and IAM authorization for HTTP APIs.

questions.questionText: A company wants to enhance a large language model (LLM) for content moderation within 3 months. The company wants the model to moderate content in accordance with the company's values and ethics. The LLM must also be capable of handling emerging trends and new forms of problematic content. Which solution will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Conduct continuous pre-training on a large amount of text-based internet content.
B. Create a high quality dataset of historical moderation decisions.
C. Fine-tune the LLM on a diverse set of general ethical guidelines from various sources.
D. Conduct reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) by using real-time input from skilled moderators.
questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) aligns model behavior with human preferences by using feedback in the reward signal. Real-time feedback from skilled moderators can express the company’s moderation values and continually incorporate newly emerging forms of problematic content.
